newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Dec 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Dec 10.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on December 10. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Indonesia's national parliament passed the country's first broadcasting bill on Monday giving the government new powers to regulate the television and radio industry as well as other electronic media such as cable television and the Internet.

A senior customs official says smugglers of the designer drug ecstasy prefer to use the country's post offices as a way of smuggling the pills into Indonesia. In 1996, 115,874 pills of ecstasy and 1.8 kg of heroine have been seized in the nation's major post offices, he said.

Indonesian President Suharto said at the opening of the Organisation of the Islamic Conference (OIC) that to achieve lasting peace in the Middle East, Israel must withdraw from the Golan Heights in Syria and Southern Lebanon.
The Indonesian government has threatened to bring the United States and Japan to the World Trade Organization (WTO) over the treatment of its hardwood and softwood exports to both countries.
